**Finding: Compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

I reviewed the fee architecture (Article V user-fee bands, p0050–p0070), the "Supplemental Payments" definition and enhancements section (p0074–p0084), support fees (p0086–p0095), the term/termination provisions (Articles IV, XIX–XXI) and general provisions. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "minimum", "damages", "interest" and "equal to" returned no Customer-payable stipulated sum.

Key points:
- No liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, minimum commitment or accelerated-fee provision is payable by us. All amounts we owe are usage- or service-based consideration.
- Article IV (p0049) preserves only Licensor's right to payment for trades actually performed on early termination — no acceleration of remaining term fees; Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return and certification duties.
- Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party, which works in our favour.
- Two near-misses are not LDs against us: the audit cost-shift on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is ordinary audit cost allocation, and the payment floor in p0070 simply ties fees to recorded traded volume. The rebate/share mechanics (p0076) run to us and are welcome.

No redline proposed. Two items are worth picking up under other rules rather than this one: the audit cost-shift trigger in p0064, and the apparent drafting slip in p0070 which states the floor applies to amounts "payable by the Licensor" where the payer is us.
